content.text:
**Resubmitted — T4C: deviation (preferred level).**

Repair made in operative language: the inserted § 11.2A now identifies the terminating party expressly as the Customer — "Corio, as the Customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One" — which cures the "Customer convenience termination present" check without altering the substance, notice period, or refund basis. The insertion carries the section number 11.2A so it sits between § 11.2 (Termination) and the existing § 11.3 (Effect of Termination) without colliding with that numbering or creating a dangling cross-reference.

Everything else is unchanged and validated (`ok:true`, minimality clean):
- One concise insertion for a genuinely absent clause; §§ 11.1 and 11.2 reproduced verbatim, hyphenation artefacts intact.
- No "in whole or in part", no survival tail, no procedure or damages boilerplate.
- Element 4 remains **already_met** on the verbatim § 11.2 quote (Commerce One's termination rights are confined to breach and insolvency); the § 11.1 non-renewal notice stays under RENEWAL and is not double-flagged.
